original_question: Let H be a Hilbert space over C and let A : D(A) ⊆ H → H be the infinitisimal generator of a bounded semigroup on H. Assume further that A−1 exists as a densely defined, closed operator. Is A−1 the infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1 ("Inverse generator problem"), which asks exactly whether the inverse of a generator of a bounded semigroup on a complex Hilbert space is again a generator of a bounded semigroup. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended problem almost verbatim: the ambient space is a Hilbert space over C, A is the infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup on H, one assumes that A^{-1} exists as a densely defined closed operator, and the question is whether A^{-1} is again the infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
missing_details: To make it fully stand-alone, the semigroup should be named as a bounded C0-semigroup (or one-parameter strongly continuous semigroup) (T(t))_{t>=0} of bounded linear operators on H, with boundedness understood as sup_{t>=0} ||T(t)|| < infinity. The paper's abstract sets this global semigroup-theoretic scope. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2410.00416))

The hypothesis that A^{-1} 'exists as a densely defined, closed operator' should be unpacked: A is injective, Ran(A) is dense in H, and the inverse A^{-1}: Ran(A) -> D(A) is closed. This is implicit in the paper's wording but useful in a stand-alone statement. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))

The paper keeps the question specifically in the Hilbert-space setting; its comments note that the Banach-space version is false and that the Hilbert-space contraction-semigroup case is already positive, so the refined question should neither broaden to Banach spaces nor narrow to contraction semigroups. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))

The paper formulates this as an open problem labeled 'Problem 1 (Inverse generator problem)', not as a broader Cayley-transform or stability question, so the sharpened version should preserve that exact scope. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
refined_question: Inverse generator problem. Let H be a complex Hilbert space, and let (T(t))_{t>=0} be a bounded C0-semigroup on H, i.e. a one-parameter strongly continuous semigroup of bounded linear operators with sup_{t>=0} ||T(t)|| < infinity, whose infinitesimal generator is A: D(A) ⊆ H -> H. Assume that A is injective and that Ran(A) is dense in H, so that the inverse operator A^{-1}: Ran(A) -> D(A) is a densely defined closed operator. Must A^{-1} be the infinitesimal generator of a bounded C0-semigroup on H? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
justification: This rewrite stays essentially verbatim to Section 1, Problem 1, while spelling out only the two implicit items needed for a stand-alone question: what 'bounded semigroup' means in the paper's C0-semigroup setting, and how to read the existence of A^{-1} as an unbounded inverse on Ran(A). I did not add any alternate formulation, because the nearby comment says only that there is a 'strong relation' to power-boundedness of the Cayley transform; it does not state an equivalence in the paper itself. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
